Siding Contractors Serving Kennewick and the Tri-Cities

Drive through any Kennewick neighborhood built before 1990 and you can read the sun's path on the houses: south and west walls faded two shades lighter than the north side, vinyl panels gone chalky and brittle, T1-11 plywood siding with checking cracks that open a little wider every summer. Kennewick's high-desert climate is hard on siding in a specific way — it's not moisture that gets it, it's ultraviolet radiation, 100°F thermal expansion cycles, and wind-driven dust that scours finishes.

Siding in Kennewick: what to know

Brittle siding and wind are a bad pairing. Vinyl that has baked for fifteen summers loses the flexibility it needs to absorb a gust or a flying branch, so wind events leave cracked panels and popped corners across town. And because siding failure here is gradual fading and embrittlement rather than dramatic rot, many homeowners live with it for years past the point where replacement would have improved both curb appeal and insulation.

We can put you in touch with siding contractors who work Kennewick, Richland, and Pasco regularly — for a single-wall repair after a windstorm or a full residing in fiber cement, vinyl, or engineered wood.

Common siding situations in Kennewick

UV-chalked and faded vinyl

Older vinyl siding develops a powdery chalk layer as UV breaks down the surface. Wipe a finger across it: if it comes back white, the material is well into its decline. Chalked vinyl can't be meaningfully painted with ordinary paint and is usually a replacement conversation.

Cracked panels from wind and thermal shock

A cold snap after a warm afternoon, or one good gust with debris in it, will crack embrittled panels — most often on west-facing walls. Single-panel replacement is possible if the profile is still manufactured, but faded surroundings mean the patch rarely matches.

Splitting T1-11 on mid-century homes

Kennewick's post-war ranch housing stock carries a lot of T1-11 and board siding. Decades of desert drying open the grain, paint fails in sheets, and the bottom edges wick sprinkler water — the one moisture source this climate reliably provides. Localized replacement plus a proper repaint often buys another decade.

How it works

  1. 1

    Walkaround and moisture check

    The contractor inspects all four exposures — sun damage varies wall by wall here — and probes bottom edges near irrigation heads, the most common hidden-damage spot in this climate.

  2. 2

    Material recommendation with sun in mind

    You'll get options rated for this exposure: fiber cement handles UV and heat exceptionally well; newer vinyl formulations resist fade far better than 1990s product; engineered wood needs a quality repaint cycle but suits the local look.

  3. 3

    Quote covering trim, wrap, and disposal

    A complete quote includes house wrap or rain screen, window and corner trim, caulking, and haul-away. Ask whether old siding disposal is included — tear-off tonnage fees are a real line item.

  4. 4

    Installation

    A typical single-story Kennewick home resides in three to five working days. Crews here often start at dawn in summer to get off west walls before afternoon heat makes materials too hot to handle.

What siding costs in Kennewick

Siding cost in Kennewick is driven mostly by material choice and how much trim and repair work hides under the old cladding. Vinyl remains the budget option; fiber cement runs half again to double vinyl's price but is the better match for this UV environment and holds paint for 12–15 years; engineered wood lands between. Homes with sprinkler-damaged sheathing at the base of walls should budget for some sheet replacement, which is only discoverable at tear-off. Wind-storm panel repairs are cheap by comparison, but expect a color mismatch on faded walls.

Frequently asked questions

Which siding holds up best against Kennewick sun?

Fiber cement is the standout — the material itself is immune to UV, and factory finishes carry 15-year fade warranties. Light colors in any material also age far better here; dark vinyl in full southern exposure is the worst-case combination.

Can I replace just the sun-damaged wall?

Yes, and it's a common request in the Tri-Cities. The trade-off is color match: a new south wall next to fifteen-year-old siding will be visibly newer. Some owners re-side the two sun-hit walls and repaint the rest.

Does new siding help with cooling costs?

It can. Adding foam-backed siding or a continuous insulation layer during residing tightens the wall assembly, and lighter reflective colors reduce wall heat gain — worth real money in a town with weeks of 95–105°F summer highs.

How do I check if a siding contractor is legitimate in Washington?

Look up their contractor registration on the WA Department of Labor & Industries site. Registration requires a bond and insurance. A registration number should appear on their bid, contract, and advertising.

Is there a bad season for siding work here?

Deep winter cold snaps make vinyl brittle to install, and 100°F-plus afternoons cause expansion issues if panels are nailed tight. Local crews work year-round but favor spring and fall for full residing jobs.
